key_insight: Deeper gradient-trained parameterized quantum circuits can improve unseen-data performance, showing double descent rather than the usual “bigger is worse” trend.
engineering_relevance: This suggests scaling PQC depth/parameters may be a viable design strategy for quantum ML systems when guided by training dynamics and validation curves.
method: Derived analytical generalization behavior using add-one-in perturbation techniques.
Linked the scaling result to spectral properties of random matrices.
Validated the theory with numerical experiments on re-uploading PQCs.
evidence_signal: Across multiple datasets and training set sizes, the experiments consistently showed the predicted double descent behavior in re-uploading PQCs.
watch_item: The result is encouraging but does not remove other practical barriers in quantum ML, so gains may still depend on circuit design, optimization, and noise.
paper_title: Cautious optimism for deep parameterized quantum circuits
